en: The Two Dyads on Limited States, Hetuduka (The Dyad on Roots)
Dependent on a state that is neither limited nor root-cause, a sublime state that is a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Eleven with respect to root, eleven with respect to object, nine with respect to predominance … pe … nine with respect to prenascence and repetition … pe … eleven with respect to non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that has neither limited nor root-cause objects, a state that has limited objects and is a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to cause, there are thirteen; with respect to object, thirteen; with respect to predominance, nine …pe… with respect to prenascence and repetition, nine …pe… with respect to non-disappearance, thirteen.
